evals.prompt: Build me a 60-card kitchen-table deck from my Moxfield collection export at evals/files/collection.csv. I mostly play casual 1v1 with friends, no sideboard needed. Pick whatever colours the collection supports best and playtest it.
evals.expected_output: One exactly-60-card decklist (Moxfield-importable .txt) plus a single self-contained HTML report in a run folder; the deck passes validate_deck.py with --deck-size 60, has a 4-of-heavy constructed shape (~22-26 lands, bell curve), goldfish statistics and narrated games, copy-count rationale and land math sections.
expectations: A '<Run Name> Deck Build <timestamp>' run folder exists in the project directory
Exactly one HTML report was produced
Report is self-contained (no external src/href to http(s) resources)
Report contains goldfish playtest statistics (keepable-hand and mulligan rates)
Report has an iteration log section
Report narrates sample games including a hostile scenario
Report lists cards that just missed the cut
transcript.md records running validate_deck.py and goldfish.py
Exported list passes validate_deck.py --format kitchen --deck-size 60 (ownership, copies, size)
Land count is in the constructed range 20-27
Constructed shape: at least 4 distinct nonbasic cards run as 4-ofs
Report has a copy-count rationale section (why each card's count)
Report has a land-math section with hypergeometric odds
Report states which format the list is legal in / legality snapshot

evals.prompt: Using my collection (evals/files/collection.csv, Moxfield export), make me a Standard-legal 60-card deck with a 15-card sideboard and tell me how to sideboard against aggro and control.
evals.expected_output: A 60 + 15 Standard-legal list validated by the cache's legalities field, sideboard guide table with In/Out per archetype, exported decklist and HTML report.
